summary: The note describes how retirees in a local neighborhood are turning to volunteering as a way to find purpose, new skills and social connection. It profiles five retirees (Maria Gonzalez, James Peterson, Linda Smith, Carl Jennings, Anne Kim) who began volunteering from September to December 2023. The main themes are self-discovery, combating isolation, the mutual benefit of giving, and the lasting community impact of service.
one_line: Retirees in a local neighborhood find purpose, new skills, friendships and lasting impact through volunteering, as shown by five profiled volunteers.
key_facts: Since September 2023 there has been a notable upswing in retirees volunteering their free time in the neighborhood.
Maria Gonzalez, a retired schoolteacher, began volunteering at the local food bank on October 5th, 2023.
Maria Gonzalez said she wanted to ensure "no one in our community goes to bed hungry."
James Peterson, a former finance manager, discovered a knack for carpentry after joining a program that builds housing for those in need on November 22nd, 2023.
James Peterson had no prior construction experience before joining the housing program.
Linda Smith, a retired attorney, volunteers in legal aid and began on September 15th, 2023; her social circle has expanded since.
Linda Smith described her volunteer relationships as "like discovering a new family you never knew you had."
Carl Jennings, a retired postal worker, volunteers with the local literacy program helping adults learn to read and write.
Carl Jennings says volunteering gives structure to his days and helps him sleep well at night.
Researchers have found that volunteering can bolster life satisfaction and positively affect mental health.
Anne Kim started teaching basic computer skills at the local community center on December 1st, 2023.
Anne Kim says teaching one person computer skills can open job opportunities that change a whole family's future.
Volunteering helps combat the isolation and loneliness that can accompany retirement.
